condition: Head injury in an anticoagulated older adult
summary: 82-year-old woman on apixaban for AF tripped on a rug 3 h ago and hit her forehead: no loss of consciousness, no amnesia, no vomiting, GCS 15, forehead haematoma.

inputs.hpi: Tripped over a rug at home 3 hours ago and hit her forehead on the floor. No loss of consciousness, remembers the whole event, no vomiting, mild local headache only. No dizziness or palpitations before the fall. Takes apixaban 5 mg twice daily for atrial fibrillation; last dose this morning.

exam.general: Alert, GCS 15. HR 78 irregular, BP 152/84, RR 16, SpO2 97%.
exam.neuro: GCS 15, pupils equal and reactive, no focal deficit. 4 cm forehead haematoma. No signs of skull fracture.

inputs.socialHistory: Lives alone, independent. Two falls this year.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Head injury in a patient taking apixaban
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Minor head injury (GCS 15, no LOC or amnesia) in an 82-year-old taking apixaban. CT head within 8 hours of injury (NICE NG232); reversal agent available if bleed; falls assessment.

emergencyLevel.note: CT within 8 h of injury: same-day, not a routine booking.

mustInclude.note: Anticoagulant alone is an indication for CT head (within 8 h) in NICE NG232.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: iOS CI 2026-09-25 (run 36169134350, database mode): no investigation matched among 2 (ios.radiation)

mustInclude.note: Reversal ready if CT shows haemorrhage.

mustExclude.note: Elective peri-operative bridging advice is the wrong frame for an anticoagulated head injury.

pathway.knownGapNote: iOS CI 2026-09-25 (run 36169134350, database mode): recommended firstVisit (No previous visits on record); expected trauma

guideline.name: NICE NG232 — Head injury: assessment and early management
guideline.section: Section 1.4 (adults): CT head within 1 h for GCS <13 on initial assessment, GCS <15 at 2 h, suspected open/depressed or basal skull fracture, post-traumatic seizure, focal deficit, >1 episode of vomiting; CT within 8 h for people with no other indication who are taking anticoagulants (wording — "perform" or "consider" — to be checked against the 2023 text)
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Head injury: assessment and early management (NG232). London: NICE; 2023.

guideline.name: ATLS 10th edition — geriatric trauma
guideline.section: Chapter 11: blunted physiological response (beta-blockers, age) masks shock; "normal" blood pressure may represent hypotension; anticoagulation increases haemorrhage risk and needs early reversal; rib fractures carry higher morbidity in older patients
guideline.citation: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. ATLS Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago: ACS; 2018. Chapter 11.

guideline.name: ATLS 10th edition — head trauma
guideline.section: Chapter 6: GCS, pupils, prevention of secondary brain injury (avoid hypoxia and hypotension), CT head, early neurosurgical consultation; reverse anticoagulation in intracranial haemorrhage
guideline.citation: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. ATLS Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago: ACS; 2018. Chapter 6.

rationale: Permutation: the low-energy fall in an older anticoagulated patient with no other CT criteria. NICE NG232: CT head within 8 h for people taking anticoagulants. Tests CT recommendation, anticoagulant flagging, same-day urgency and the iOS trauma pathway for the CC "Fall at home, hit head" (no trauma keyword in the iOS list).
